package_info.why_malicious: All packages in this campaign execute obfuscated JavaScript code at install time, which collects extensive system information and establishes a reverse shell to a remote attacker-controlled server, enabling full remote code execution and exfiltration of sensitive data.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation or test script execution, the package runs ./scripts/init.js, which triggers the malicious payload regardless of how the package is installed or tested.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages rarely execute arbitrary scripts on install, especially across multiple lifecycle hooks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not run custom scripts on install/test/init unless absolutely necessary and clearly documented.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use install scripts for native module compilation, but not for launching detached processes.
key_indicators: Multiple lifecycle hooks trigger the same script
No legitimate reason for running code on install/test/init

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When triggered by install/test/init, this code launches scripts/rsh.js as a detached child process, allowing the malicious code to persist after the parent process exits.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning a detached child process during install is highly unusual and enables persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Install scripts should not launch persistent background processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, daemons or background services might be started, but this is not standard for npm packages.
key_indicators: Immediate process exit to hide activity

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects detailed system, environment, and user information, compresses it, decompresses an obfuscated payload, sets a suspicious environment variable, and executes the payload via eval.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting extensive system and environment data, obfuscating payloads, and using eval to execute code are all hallmarks of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect and exfiltrate system information or execute obfuscated code via eval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Compression and system info gathering may be used in diagnostics, but not in this context.
key_indicators: Use of eval on decompressed payload

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a persistent reverse shell to rsh.51pwn.com:8880, sends collected system info, and allows remote command execution by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing a reverse shell to an external server is a direct remote access backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should open a reverse shell or exfiltrate system data to an attacker.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; reverse shells are always malicious in this context.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering install/test/init scripts.
init.js launches rsh.js as a detached child process and exits.
rsh.js collects system, environment, and user data, decompresses and evals obfuscated payload.
Reverse shell payload connects to rsh.51pwn.com:8880, sends system info, and enables remote command execution.

behavioral_signatures: Detached child process creation in install scripts
Obfuscated or Unicode-escaped code in JavaScript files
Use of eval on decompressed or dynamically generated code
Outbound connections to hardcoded C2 domains (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com:8880)
Collection and exfiltration of system/environment/user data
file_indicators: package.json with install/test/init scripts running node
network_indicators: Outbound TCP connections to uncommon ports during install
Initial data exfiltration containing system info
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that execute scripts during install/test/init, especially those launching detached processes or containing obfuscated code. Flag any package that establishes outbound connections to suspicious domains (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com) or ports. Use static analysis to detect eval usage on dynamically decompressed payloads and the presence of Unicode-escaped code. Alert on collection and exfiltration of system/environment/user data during package installation.
